title: Augmentation normalization and resolution naturality of product internal bars
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $G,H$ be profinite groups. For $P=1,G,H,G\times H$, let $\mathcal A_P(A)$ be the category of internal $A$-modules with an $A$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline P$, with the inflation adjunctions of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Internal modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; write $U_P:\mathcal A_P(A)\to\mathcal A_1(A)$ for forgetting the action, $A[S]$ for the free internal module on a profinite set $S$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction], and $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ for the internal module Hom [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].
Let $N\in\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ and let $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ be a nonnegative injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Use ordinary K-injective derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and write $Q$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.
Put $C^{a,b,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a\times H^b],U_{G\times H}I^q)$ for $a,b,q\geq0$. In each group direction use inhomogeneous bar cofaces (first face acts on the coefficient, interior faces multiply adjacent parameters, final face drops the last parameter) and codegeneracies inserting the identity. Write $D=\operatorname{Tot}_{n,q}C^{n,n,q}$ with differential $\delta_{\rm diag}+(-1)^nd_q$, and $T=\operatorname{Tot}_{a,b,q}C$ with differential $\delta_G+(-1)^a\delta_H+(-1)^{a+b}d_q$; totals have finite sums in each degree [def-sp-double-complex-total].
Define $K^{a,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],(I^q)^H)$, $L=\operatorname{Tot}_{a,q}K$ with differential $\delta_G+(-1)^ad_q$, and $J^\bullet=(I^\bullet)^{G\times H}$. Let $j_D:J^\bullet\to D$, $j_K:J^\bullet\to L$ and $k:L\to T$ be the invariant inclusions supported in group degree zero, in $a=0$, and in $b=0$, respectively. Assume these three maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and that $I^\bullet$ and $(I^\bullet)^H$ are K-injective in their action categories. Let $S:D\to T$ be the codegeneracy shuffle specified in [lem-sfb-bicosimplicial-shuffle-totalization]. Then $S j_D=k j_K$ as chain maps. In $D(\mathcal A_1(A))$, $Q(S)=Q(kj_K)Q(j_D)^{-1}$ is the unique arrow with this augmentation identity and is the augmented product-nerve comparison with $H$ first. Under the canonical K-injective identifications of $Q(J^\bullet)$ with the direct and successive derived invariants, this arrow is exactly the conjugate derived-adjunction comparison induced by $M^{G\times H}=(M^H)^G$ and the specified inflation adjunctions.
For every equivariant map $N\to N'$ and every lift between two nonnegative equivariant injective resolutions, postcomposition gives maps of $C,K,J,D,L,T$ commuting with $j_D,j_K,k,S$. The two normalized derived-object identifications and the comparison arrow commute with these maps. Any two lifts induce the same derived arrows: a resolution homotopy induces total homotopies with signs $(-1)^{a+b}$ on $C^{a,b,q}$, $(-1)^a$ on $K^{a,q}$ and $(-1)^n$ on $C^{n,n,q}$. The resulting identifications are independent of the chosen resolutions, using lifts of the identity for a change of resolution. These assertions also hold when a group is trivial (using its unnormalized constant nerve) or $N=0$ (using the zero resolution).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-condensed-product-bar-resolution-model], the specified internal Hom terms and bar operators form a bicosimplicial nonnegative complex, with commuting group directions and resolution differential. Its hypotheses are precisely the coefficient category, groups and nonnegative equivariant injective resolution in the statement. We use only this structural assertion, not its augmentation quasi-isomorphism conclusion. The category $\mathcal A_1(A)$ is abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Thus the shuffle theorem applies to $X=C$. The totals in the item are exactly its $D(X),T(X)$, with the same signs and finite sums [def-sp-double-complex-total].

proof.text: For the invariant inclusion $i:J\to C^{0,0,\bullet}=UI^\bullet$, both group differentials vanish: their degree-zero formulas are $g\cdot m-m$ and $h\cdot m-m$. Apply the augmentation clause of [lem-sfb-bicosimplicial-shuffle-totalization] to $i$. Its map $j_T$ is $kj_K$, since both are the same invariant inclusion in $(a,b)=(0,0)$ and zero elsewhere. Hence $Sj_D=kj_K$ strictly. Equivalently, on the only nonzero group-degree component of $j_D$ the shuffle has $n=0$; its unique empty partition has sign $+1$ and both surjections are identities. This also specifies the augmented product-nerve comparison, with the $G$ direction outside the $H$ direction.

proof.text: Write $e_D=Q(j_D)$ and $e_T=Q(kj_K)$. Both are invertible by the assumed quasi-isomorphisms and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Applying $Q$ to Step 2 gives $Q(S)e_D=e_T$, hence $Q(S)=e_Te_D^{-1}$. Every arrow $u:Q(D)\to Q(T)$ with $ue_D=e_T$ equals this expression by right composition with $e_D^{-1}$. These are arrows between the full derived objects.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] with $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C)=(\mathcal A_1(A),\mathcal A_G(A),\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A))$. Its $L_a$ is trivial inflation to $G$, $L_b$ is projection inflation to $G\times H$, and $L_c$ is direct trivial inflation. All are exact additive, and their specified right adjoints and composite-left identity are supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. The underived conjugate is $\kappa:M^{G\times H}\to(M^H)^G$, the identity on invariant sections. The common resolution $I$ and $I^H$ are K-injective as assumed. Consequently, if $\beta_c:QJ\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{G\times H}(N[0])$ and $\beta_{ab}:QJ\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$ are the canonical computation identifications of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the derived conjugate $c$ satisfies $c\beta_c=\beta_{ab}Q(C(\kappa)_I)=\beta_{ab}$. Define the two normalized identifications by $\rho_D=\beta_ce_D^{-1}$ and $\rho_T=\beta_{ab}e_T^{-1}$. Step 3 gives $\rho_TQ(S)=\beta_{ab}e_D^{-1}=c\rho_D$. This proves the claimed adjunction normalization, with its specified units and counits.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; specialization of the normalized composition theorem to exact trivial and projection inflation.

proof.text: Let $f:N\to N'$ and $v:I\to I'$ lift $f$. In $C^{a,b,q}$ postcompose with $Uv^q$; in $K^{a,q}$ postcompose with $(v^q)^H$; in $J$ restrict $v^q$ to full invariants. These maps exist since $v^q$ is equivariant. They commute with $d_q$ since $v$ is a chain map. They commute with all group operators: equivariance handles the first face, and for any parameter substitution $t$, $v\circ(F\circ t)=(v\circ F)\circ t$ handles interior faces, final faces and identity insertions. Invariant inclusions commute because they leave a section unchanged. Thus the induced maps of $D,L,T$ commute with $j_D,j_K,k$. Every component of $S$ is a finite signed sum of such parameter substitutions, so it commutes as well. Internal Hom postcomposition preserves sums: by the closed adjunction its transpose is coefficient evaluation followed by the given map, and evaluation and composition are additive [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. These formulas concern morphisms of internal modules, so remain valid after every profinite base change.

proof.text: The computation identifications $\beta_c,\beta_{ab}$ in Step 4 commute with a lift $v$: the computation unit $\eta$ in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] is natural, so for any termwise functor $F$ it gives $RF(Qv)\eta_I=\eta_{I'}Q(Fv)$. Compose this equation with the localized augmentation $N[0]\to I$ and its counterpart for $N'$, and invert their quasi-isomorphisms. For successive invariants apply this first to $(-)^H$ and then to $(-)^G$; all the needed computation units are invertible on $I,I^H$ and the corresponding primed complexes. Combining these equations with the augmentation squares of Step 5, and inverting $e_D,e_T$, gives naturality of $\rho_D,\rho_T$. The naturality of $c$ is also part of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization]; equivalently it follows from $c=\beta_{ab}\beta_c^{-1}$. Hence the comparison arrow commutes with every lift.

proof.text: Lifts exist by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists], applied in the abelian product-action category. If $v,w:I\to I'$ lift the same $f$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] with $\alpha:N[0]\to I$ and target $I'$. Here $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $I'$ is bounded below and termwise injective in that very category, and $v\alpha=w\alpha$. We obtain equivariant maps $h^q:I^q\to I'^{q-1}$ with $v-w=d_{I'}h+hd_I$. In particular $h^0=0$, since the resolutions vanish below zero.

source.place: Tags 013P and 013S, lemma-morphisms-lift and lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, applied in the condensed product-action category.

proof.text: Postcompose with $h$ in each internal Hom and restrict it to invariant submodules. Write the resulting degree $-1$ maps as $\widehat h_C,\widehat h_K,\widehat h_J$. They commute with every group operator by the same explicit parameter-substitution and equivariance identities in Step 5. On $T$ put $H_T|_{C^{a,b,q}}=(-1)^{a+b}\widehat h_C$, on $L$ put $H_L|_{K^{a,q}}=(-1)^a\widehat h_K$, on $D$ put $H_D|_{C^{n,n,q}}=(-1)^n\widehat h_C$, and on $J$ put $H_J=\widehat h_J$. For $T$, the $G$ terms in $dH_T+H_Td$ have coefficients $(-1)^{a+b}$ and $(-1)^{a+b+1}$, and the $H$ terms have coefficients $(-1)^b$ and $(-1)^{b+1}$; thus they cancel. The internal terms have coefficient $(-1)^{2(a+b)}=1$ and equal postcomposition with $d_{I'}h+hd_I=v-w$. For $D,L$ the identical expansion with group degree $n,a$ gives cancellation coefficients $(-1)^r,(-1)^{r+1}$ and internal coefficient $1$. For $J$ just restrict the original homotopy equation. Therefore these are homotopies between all the induced total maps. They agree on the invariant augmentations, and $H_TS=SH_D$ since every shuffle component has $a+b=n$. The finite sums ensure that each displayed map is defined in every degree. Homotopic maps become equal under $Q$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For two resolutions of $N$, choose lifts of $1_N$ in both directions using Step 7. Their composites lift $1_N$ and hence are homotopic to the respective identities by the uniqueness result in that step. Step 8 makes their maps on $J,D,L,T$ inverse isomorphisms after localization. For three resolutions, a composite of identity lifts and a direct identity lift induce the same arrows, again by Steps 7–8. Thus the identifications are independent of the resolution, with the required transitivity, and the naturality squares of Steps 5–6 persist under any such change. No step requires a nontrivial group: for a trivial factor the unnormalized nerve retains one identity map in every degree, and the same face, shuffle and sign formulas still apply. For $N=0$ take $I=0$; all terms and maps are zero. Other resolutions of zero are covered by the identity-lift argument just given.
